## Why a second workflow

`Nexus — Gmail triage` is driven by a **Gmail trigger**, and a polling trigger only
fires when it has something to emit. So its `mail_sync` marker means *"the last time
mail arrived"*, never *"the last time we looked"* — and a quiet weekend is
indistinguishable from a stopped container, an expired credential, or a Mac that
never woke up.

`MailPanel` reads the newest `kind='mail_sync', status='done'` row as its freshness
signal, so that gap is exactly the conflation the whole design exists to avoid.

This workflow closes it: on a schedule it **actually calls Gmail**, then records a run
with `fetched: 0`. Calling Gmail is the point — a heartbeat that only proved n8n was
alive would keep reporting healthy while the Gmail credential silently expired. On the
free Google tier that is a real 7-day clock unless the consent screen is published.

It never ingests messages. Fetching is the trigger workflow's job, and two writers
upserting the same rows is how you get a race for no benefit.
